title: Cloud Operations Developer - Mid-level
description: Role-specific fundamentals and practical troubleshooting. 8 MCQs and 3 written scenarios; no coding questions.
reviewerInstructions: Score each written response against its rubric. Award points for specific, technically sound reasoning and trade-offs. Notes are optional. Publish only after every criterion is scored. The recommendation is a human judgment; this application does not make hiring decisions.

items.text: Which Kubernetes probe determines whether a container is ready to receive service traffic?
items.explanation: A readiness probe controls readiness for traffic; it does not by itself restart the container.

items.text: What is a primary purpose of a Kubernetes liveness probe?
choices: Detect an unhealthy container that should be restarted
items.correctAnswer: Detect an unhealthy container that should be restarted
items.explanation: A failing liveness probe can trigger a container restart.

items.text: When a startup probe is configured, when do liveness and readiness probes begin?
choices: Only after the startup probe succeeds
Only after the pod is deleted
items.correctAnswer: Only after the startup probe succeeds
items.explanation: Startup probes protect slow-starting applications from premature liveness and readiness checks.

items.text: Which access policy best follows least privilege?
choices: Grant only the actions and resources needed for its task
Share one root credential across services
items.correctAnswer: Grant only the actions and resources needed for its task
items.explanation: Least privilege restricts permissions to the resources, actions and conditions needed.

items.text: Which CloudWatch feature evaluates a metric against configured conditions and can trigger an action?
items.explanation: CloudWatch metric alarms evaluate metric data against defined conditions and can invoke configured actions.

items.text: What does a successful backup job alone prove?
choices: The application has no data loss risk
A backup was created; recovery still needs restore testing
items.correctAnswer: A backup was created; recovery still needs restore testing
items.explanation: Recovery assurance requires testing restores and validating the recovered application against recovery objectives.

items.text: After a deployment causes a sharp error-rate increase, what is the best first operational response?
choices: Follow the incident procedure, stabilize service and assess rollback
items.correctAnswer: Follow the incident procedure, stabilize service and assess rollback
items.explanation: A controlled incident response prioritizes service restoration and preserves evidence for diagnosis.

items.text: What should an alert intended to wake an on-call engineer normally indicate?
choices: An actionable symptom with meaningful service impact
items.correctAnswer: An actionable symptom with meaningful service impact
items.explanation: Actionable alerts reduce noise and direct attention to problems that require intervention.

items.text: A new deployment increases latency and HTTP 5xx errors. Walk through the first 15 minutes of incident response, including communication and rollback decisions.

rubric.label: Diagnosis and stabilization
rubric.guidance: 0: destructive speculation. 1-4: checks logs only. 5-7: correlates deployment, metrics and dependency symptoms; chooses a safe rollback or mitigation. 8-10: prioritizes impact, tests hypotheses and considers rollback risk.

rubric.label: Operational discipline
rubric.guidance: 0: no coordination. 1-4: generic status updates. 5-7: incident roles, timeline, evidence preservation and clear updates. 8-10: verification criteria, follow-up ownership and alert improvements.

items.text: A Kubernetes service intermittently sends requests to an application before it can serve them. Propose probe configuration and a safe way to verify the fix.

rubric.label: Probe semantics and application design
rubric.guidance: 0: confuses readiness and liveness. 1-4: adds a probe without reasoning. 5-7: distinguishes startup/readiness/liveness and meaningful endpoints. 8-10: handles dependency checks, false positives and timeout thresholds.

rubric.label: Safe rollout and verification
rubric.guidance: 0: direct unverified production change. 1-4: manual checks only. 5-7: staged rollout, traffic checks, events and rollback. 8-10: failure injection and monitoring for restart storms or dropped traffic.

items.text: Design recovery for a stateful service with a 15-minute recovery-point objective and a one-hour recovery-time objective. Include access control and restore testing.

rubric.label: Recovery design
rubric.guidance: 0: assumes backups equal recovery. 1-4: generic backup schedule. 5-7: maps RPO/RTO to backups, replication and runbooks. 8-10: discusses consistency, dependency recovery and realistic restore timing.

rubric.label: Security and validation
rubric.guidance: 0: no controls or tests. 1-4: mentions encryption. 5-7: least privilege, encryption, isolation and routine restore drills. 8-10: tests integrity, retention failures and recovery evidence against objectives.
